content.text: Social Geography of Andhra Pradesh and India: Demographics, Tribal Anthropology, Urbanization, and Migration Patterns

The social geography of Andhra Pradesh reflects a mature demographic transition characterized by a below-replacement fertility rate (TFR ~1.6), a favorable sex ratio exceeding national averages, significant rural-urban disparities, and a unique indigenous tribal population residing in the scheduled agency tracts of the Eastern Ghats governed by special constitutional safeguards under the Fifth Schedule.

content.text: 2. Rural-Urban Composition, Metropolitan Nodes, and Migration

items: Rural-Urban Split: Rural population constitutes 70.47% (~3.49 crore) while urban population accounts for 29.53% (~1.46 crore). Urban growth is accelerating around peri-urban corridors and industrial nodes.

Major Urban Agglomerations: (1) Visakhapatnam: Port-city, IT and industrial capital, the largest metropolis in AP (~2.3+ million); (2) Vijayawada-Guntur Agglomeration: Core commercial, transit, and agricultural hub encompassing the Amaravati Capital Region; (3) Tirupati: Global pilgrimage and electronics/manufacturing hub; (4) Kurnool and Nellore: Gateway urban centers for Rayalaseema and South Coastal AP.

Migration Dynamics: Intra-state migration flows from the rain-shadow, drought-prone Rayalaseema districts (Anantapur, Kurnool) and poverty-stricken North Coastal districts (Srikakulam, Vizianagaram) toward the irrigated deltas and coastal cities. Inter-state migration historically targets Hyderabad, Chennai, and Bengaluru. Distress international labor migration from Godavari and Rayalaseema to Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries remains prominent.

content.text: 3. Scheduled Tribes and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)

Scheduled Tribes constitute approximately 5.53% of the state's population (~27.4 lakh), primarily inhabiting the Fifth Schedule agency tracts of the Eastern Ghats. Andhra Pradesh is home to 7 designated Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs):

content.caption: Tribal Groups, PVTGs, Habitat, and Anthropological Features in Andhra Pradesh
rows: Nallamala Forest range (Palnadu, Prakasam, Nandyal, Kurnool)
One of the oldest hunter-gatherer aboriginal tribes of peninsular India; semi-nomadic, rely on minor forest produce (honey, gums, roots); worship Lord Narasimha at Srisailam (Ahobilam).
Bison Hills along the Godavari gorge (Alluri Sitharama Raju, Eluru)
Traditional slash-and-burn (Podu) cultivators; renowned for bamboo crafts and indigenous herbal knowledge; matrilineal survivals.
Pioneers of elaborate terrace cultivation and stonewall contouring on steep hill slopes; distinctive Munda linguistic branch; iconic 'Idital' pictographic wall paintings.
Famous for the traditional 'Dhemsa' circular folk dance and hand-woven Bark-fiber Kerang textiles.
Dravidian-speaking groups; practice shifting agriculture; distinct linguistic dialects (Kui/Kuvi).
Pastoral community; celebrated for vibrant needlecraft embroidery, mirror work, and Lambadi folk dances.
Plains tribal community residing near coasts and estuaries; expert rat-catchers, snake-handlers, and traditional medicinal herbalists.

items: Fifth Schedule Administration: Scheduled agency areas in AP are administered under Article 244(1) of the Constitution, granting special regulatory powers to the Governor to suspend or modify parliamentary and state legislation.

Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation (Regulation 1 of 1970 - LTR 1/70): The most stringent anti-alienation law in India; creates an absolute legal presumption that any transfer of immovable property in Scheduled Areas to a non-tribal is null and void, protecting tribal land rights.

Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA): Empowers Gram Sabhas with mandatory consultations regarding land acquisition, ownership of Minor Forest Produce (MFP), and management of water bodies.

Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs): Project-level institutional nodal agencies spearheading health, education, and livelihood interventions across major agency centers: Paderu (ASR), Rampachodavaram (ASR), Parvathipuram, Seethampeta (Srikakulam), K.R. Puram (Eluru), and Srisailam (Chenchu special project).

content.text: Part A: Mains Analytical & Descriptive Questions

items:
Analyze the demographic profile of Andhra Pradesh with special focus on literacy disparities, declining fertility rates, and their long-term socioeconomic implications. (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Highlight key metrics (TFR ~1.6, lower decadal growth of 9.21%, favorable sex ratio 997); examine educational bottlenecks (total literacy 67.35% trailing national average of 74%, persistent female literacy gap of ~15%, acute tribal agency backwardness); discuss impending demographic aging (shrinking working-age cohort, rising dependency ratio of elderly population, rising demand for geriatric care and social security pensions); conclude with policy recommendations (investing in secondary/vocational education quality, skill development to capture the remaining demographic dividend window).

Examine the socio-economic conditions of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in Andhra Pradesh. Evaluate the effectiveness of constitutional and statutory safeguards in protecting their habitat. (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Identify the 7 PVTGs (Chenchus, Konda Reddis, Savaras, Gadabas, Porjas, Kondhs, Thotis); detail vulnerabilities (declining or stagnant population, pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, acute malnutrition, reliance on dwindling forest produce); evaluate protective legal frameworks: Fifth Schedule, PESA 1996, and AP Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1970 (1/70 Act prohibiting land transfers); discuss ground realities (non-tribal encroachment, displacement from mining/irrigation projects like Polavaram, implementation gaps of Forest Rights Act 2006); emphasize community-driven conservation and ITDA empowerment.

Discuss the pattern and causes of rural-to-urban and distress inter-state migration from Andhra Pradesh. (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Categorize migration patterns: internal distress migration from rain-shadow Rayalaseema and drought-hit Anantapur/Prakasam; seasonal agrarian migration to coastal deltas; youth urbanization toward Visakhapatnam, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru for service/IT jobs; gulf migration from Godavari/Kadapa for construction/domestic labor; analyze root drivers: recurrent droughts, lack of industrial employment in interior districts, and agrarian distress; suggest solutions: rural non-farm employment, value-added agro-processing, and balanced regional industrialization.

content.text: Part B: Screening / Prelims Objective Questions

items:
Q1. According to the 2011 Census, what was the overall Sex Ratio (females per 1,000 males) in Andhra Pradesh?
(a) 943
(b) 970
(c) 997
(d) 1005
Correct Answer: (c) 997 [Explanation: In the 2011 Census, Andhra Pradesh recorded an overall sex ratio of 997 females per 1,000 males, notably higher than the all-India national average of 943.]

Q2. Which district in Andhra Pradesh records the lowest population density according to the 2011 Census data?
(a) Anantapur
(b) YSR Kadapa
(c) Srikakulam
(d) Alluri Sitharama Raju / Eastern Ghats agency
Correct Answer: (d) Alluri Sitharama Raju / Eastern Ghats agency [Explanation: The tribal agency hill tracts (now organized into Alluri Sitharama Raju district) record the lowest density in the state due to rugged mountainous terrain and dense forest cover.]

Q3. Which of the following indigenous tribal communities of Andhra Pradesh is formally classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG)?
(a) Sugali / Lambadi
(b) Yerukula
(c) Konda Reddi
(d) Valmiki
Correct Answer: (c) Konda Reddi [Explanation: Konda Reddis, inhabiting the hill tracts along the Godavari river, are recognized as one of the 7 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in Andhra Pradesh.]

Q4. The landmark 'Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1970' (LTR 1/70) provides that:
(a) Tribals can freely sell agricultural lands to corporate industries
(b) Any transfer of land in Scheduled Areas in favor of a non-tribal is presumed null and void
(c) Only national banks can acquire tribal mortgages
(d) Non-tribals can purchase land with Tahsildar approval
Correct Answer: (b) Any transfer of land in Scheduled Areas in favor of a non-tribal is presumed null and void [Explanation: Regulation 1 of 1970 created an absolute legal presumption prohibiting transfer of immovable property in Scheduled Areas to any person who is not a member of a Scheduled Tribe.]

Q5. Which tribal group in the Nallamala forest region of Andhra Pradesh is traditionally associated with Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy and Bhramaramba at Srisailam?
(a) Chenchu
(b) Savara
(c) Gadaba
(d) Porja
Correct Answer: (a) Chenchu [Explanation: The Chenchu tribe lives in the Nallamala forests and shares a revered spiritual association with the Srisailam temple, revering Chenchu Lakshmi as an incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi.]
